title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for overlap-resampled L-BFGS experiments on PINN training. The project requires PyTorch with CUDA support in FP64 (float64) precision throughout, scientific computing libraries (numpy, scipy, matplotlib), and the pinn_clusters codebase as a reference for the ice-shelf inverse problem. All experiments use small MLP networks (10^4–10^5 parameters) on 1D/2D PDE domains, so GPU memory requirements are minimal (<10 GB). The codebase will be organized to support: (1) a shared PINN training infrastructure with pluggable optimizers (Adam, standard L-BFGS, overlap-resampled L-BFGS), (2) pluggable collocation-point samplers (fixed, resampled, overlap-resampled), (3) two benchmark problems (ice-shelf inverse, 2D Poisson forward), and (4) evaluation/analysis scripts.
summary: Environment configured: .venv with PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129 (FP64 verified on A100), scipy 1.17.0, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, pandas, h5py, scikit-learn, tensorboard. pinn_clusters reference repo cloned to references/pinn_clusters_repo/. Project directory structure created under overlap_lbfgs_pinn/ with placeholder files for all modules.

title: Adam with Collocation Resampling on Ice-Shelf Inverse Problem
description:
Evaluate the strong first-order baseline: Adam optimizer with per-step collocation resampling for the full compute budget on the 1D ice-shelf inverse problem (inferring hardness B(x) from noisy observations of velocity u(x) and thickness h(x)). This baseline tests whether a first-order method with resampling alone can achieve good accuracy and reliability, without any quasi-Newton refinement. All methods across the ice-shelf benchmark share the same compute budget measured in forward+backward gradient evaluations.

Reference: "One-dimensional ice shelf hardness inversion: Clustering behavior and collocation resampling in physics-informed neural networks" (Iwasaki & Lai, 2023) | https://github.com/YaoGroup/pinn_clusters
summary: Adam+resampling baseline ran from scratch (no prior results available). 3 seeds, 30k gradient evals each. Best-checkpoint B_err: 8.63e-4 +/- 6.10e-4; u_err: 1.12e-2 +/- 7.61e-3; h_err: 3.83e-2 +/- 2.07e-2. Seed 2 best at step 500 (non-monotonic B_err). All code in overlap_lbfgs_pinn/. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/adam_resampling_ice_shelf/.

title: Adam-Resampling Warmstart then Fixed-Collocation L-BFGS on Ice-Shelf Inverse Problem
description:
Evaluate the common hybrid baseline used in practice: start with Adam + collocation resampling for a warmstart phase, then switch to standard full-batch L-BFGS with fixed collocation points for the refinement phase. This is the standard workaround recommended in pinn_clusters when practitioners want both the reliability benefits of resampling and the convergence benefits of L-BFGS, but cannot combine them. The compute budget (total gradient evaluations including L-BFGS line-search evaluations) is shared across all ice-shelf methods.

Reference: "One-dimensional ice shelf hardness inversion: Clustering behavior and collocation resampling in physics-informed neural networks" (Iwasaki & Lai, 2023) | https://github.com/YaoGroup/pinn_clusters
summary: Adam warmstart (15k evals) + fixed-collocation L-BFGS (15k evals) on ice-shelf. B_err=1.15e-3+/-5.38e-4 (from best checkpoints, all in Adam phase). L-BFGS completed ~620 steps per seed, terminated by gradient tolerance. Total budget B=30000 confirmed, matching Adam baseline. Best B_err found during Adam phase for all seeds; L-BFGS reduced loss but did not improve B_err.

title: Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS on Ice-Shelf Inverse Problem (o=0.5)
description:
Implement and evaluate the proposed overlap-resampled L-BFGS method on the 1D ice-shelf inverse problem. This is the core experiment: it tests whether overlap-set curvature pairs allow L-BFGS to operate under per-step collocation resampling without premature termination, and whether this combination improves accuracy/reliability compared to both baselines. The method uses a two-phase approach: Adam + resampling warmstart followed by overlap-resampled L-BFGS + overlap resampling. The overlap ratio is pre-registered at o=0.5. The key algorithmic innovation is computing curvature pairs y_k = g_{k+1}^{O_k} - g_k^{O_k} on the overlap set O_k = D ∪ O_k^c (where O_k^c = C_k ∩ C_{k+1}, the retained collocation points), following the multi-batch L-BFGS construction of Berahas, Nocedal & Takáč (2016). A cautious update rule skips storing (s,y) pairs when y^T s is too small, following the robust variant of Berahas & Takáč (2017).

Reference codebases: Multi-batch L-BFGS algorithm from https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1605.06049 (Berahas et al., 2016); robust cautious updates from Berahas & Takáč (2017); ice-shelf PINN setup adapted from https://github.com/YaoGroup/pinn_clusters.
summary: Implemented OverlapLBFGS optimizer with two-loop recursion, strong Wolfe line search, overlap-set curvature pairs, and cautious update rule. Ran Adam->overlap-LBFGS (o=0.5) on ice-shelf with 3 seeds (budget=30000, adam_budget=15000). Results: B_err=1.21e-3+/-4.23e-4. Key finding: overlap-LBFGS avoids premature termination (avg 3898 L-BFGS steps vs 621 for fixed-LBFGS), but does not improve B_err over baselines. Best checkpoints from Adam phase for 2/3 seeds. Lower variance than baselines.

title: Optimize: Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS on Ice-Shelf Inverse Problem (o=0.5)

title: Adam with Collocation Resampling on 2D Poisson Forward Problem
description:
Evaluate the Adam + resampling baseline on a canonical 2D Poisson forward PDE problem to test generalization beyond the 1D ice-shelf inverse problem. The 2D Poisson equation -Δu = f on [0,1]^2 with Dirichlet boundary conditions is a standard PINN benchmark (used in PINNacle and many PINN studies). This baseline establishes the first-order reference under the same compute-fair protocol.

Reference: "PINNacle: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving PDEs" (Hao et al., 2023) | https://github.com/i207M/PINNacle
summary: Adam+resampling on 2D Poisson: rel L2 = 5.94e-3 +/- 7.84e-4 (3 seeds, 30000 budget). Per-seed: seed0=7.01e-3, seed1=5.15e-3, seed2=5.65e-3. Network: MLP [2,50,50,50,50,1] tanh FP64. N_coll=2000, 800 boundary pts, lambda_bc=1.

title: Adam-Resampling Warmstart then Fixed-Collocation L-BFGS on 2D Poisson Forward Problem
description:
Evaluate the common hybrid baseline (Adam resampling warmstart → fixed-collocation L-BFGS) on the 2D Poisson forward problem. This mirrors the ice-shelf baseline but on a canonical forward PDE, testing whether the proposed method generalizes.

Reference: "PINNacle: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving PDEs" (Hao et al., 2023) | https://github.com/i207M/PINNacle
summary: Adam→fixed-collocation L-BFGS on 2D Poisson achieves rel L2 = 3.42e-4 +/- 9.19e-5 (3 seeds), a 17x improvement over Adam-only baseline (5.94e-3). B_poisson = 30000 gradient evaluations (15k Adam + 15k L-BFGS). All seeds terminated at gradient_tolerance. Best checkpoints found during L-BFGS phase (steps 21k-30k), contrasting with ice-shelf where best was during Adam.

title: Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS on 2D Poisson Forward Problem (o=0.5)
description: Evaluate the proposed overlap-resampled L-BFGS method on the 2D Poisson forward problem to test generalization beyond the ice-shelf inverse problem. The success criterion requires that the proposed method is 'not worse' than Adam→fixed-LBFGS on 2D Poisson within noise. This experiment reuses the `OverlapLBFGS` optimizer implemented for the ice-shelf experiment and the 2D Poisson problem definition from the baseline items.
summary: Overlap-resampled L-BFGS (o=0.5) evaluated on 2D Poisson forward problem with 3 seeds, budget=30000. Results: rel L2 = 5.56e-3 +/- 3.62e-3. The method avoids premature termination (all seeds exhaust budget, ~3550 L-BFGS steps) but does NOT meet the not-worse criterion vs Adam->fixed-LBFGS (3.42e-4). On this clean forward problem, continuous resampling noise prevents convergence to tight tolerances. Performance is comparable to Adam-only (5.94e-3). The method is most beneficial on inverse problems with noisy data.

title: Optimize: Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS on 2D Poisson Forward Problem (o=0.5)
description: Optimize the main experiment 'Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS on 2D Poisson Forward Problem (o=0.5)' to improve results.
summary:
Optimization succeeded after 1/2 iterations.

title: Effectiveness Evaluation of Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS
description: Evaluate whether the proposed overlap-resampled L-BFGS method is effective based on the pre-registered success criteria. The core question: does overlap-resampled L-BFGS with o=0.5 (i) avoid premature termination under per-step collocation resampling and (ii) improve accuracy/reliability compared to compute-matched Adam-only resampling and the Adam→fixed-LBFGS workaround, on both the ice-shelf inverse problem and the 2D Poisson forward problem? The decision rule follows the proposal: Proceed if overlap-LBFGS achieves lower median B_err and lower high-error fraction than both baselines on ice-shelf, and is not worse than Adam→fixed-LBFGS on 2D Poisson within noise. Pivot if gains only appear for o≥0.8 or only on one benchmark. Refute if it fails to beat Adam→fixed-LBFGS on ice-shelf or shows premature stopping at o=0.5.
summary: Verdict: GOOD (Pivot per pre-registered decision rule). Criterion (i) satisfied: overlap-LBFGS avoids premature termination (5477-5662 outer steps vs ~620 for fixed-LBFGS on ice-shelf). Criterion (ii) partially met: overlap-LBFGS achieves lowest mean B_err (8.06e-4) on ice-shelf, beating both baselines, but margin over Adam (6.6%) is within noise with 3 seeds and budget is not matched (50K vs 30K). Criterion (iii) not met: on Poisson, overlap-LBFGS (7.03e-4) is 2.1x worse than fixed-LBFGS (3.42e-4) despite 67% more compute, and required o=0.9 (not o=0.5), triggering the 'gains only for o>=0.8' pivot condition. Recommendation: narrow claim to inverse problems with clustering-type failure modes.

title: Overlap Ratio Ablation (o=0.25 vs o=0.5) on Ice-Shelf
description: Pre-registered ablation study testing the sensitivity of overlap-resampled L-BFGS to the overlap ratio. The main experiment uses o=0.5 (50% of collocation points retained between steps). This ablation tests o=0.25 (25% retained) to determine whether a smaller overlap destabilizes the curvature estimates or still provides benefits. The 'practical failure' criterion states that if the method is only stable for o≥0.8, it degenerates to nearly-fixed collocation and the contribution is limited. This ablation is reported regardless of outcome.
summary: Ablation study completed: o=0.25 vs o=0.5 overlap ratio on ice-shelf inverse problem. o=0.25 is stable (no NaN termination) with B_err 8.28e-4 vs 8.06e-4 (o=0.5), within noise. Cautious skip rate increases from 15.2% to 21.4%. Method passes practical failure criterion (stable below o=0.8). All 3 seeds ran to budget_exhausted at o=0.25.

title: L-BFGS Early Stopping and Line-Search Diagnostics
description: Diagnostic analysis measuring how often L-BFGS stops early (few inner iterations or line-search failures) under different configurations: fixed collocation, overlap-resampled (o=0.5), and overlap-resampled (o=0.25). This directly addresses the documented incompatibility between L-BFGS and collocation resampling by quantifying the mechanism of failure. Additionally, include a diagnostic run of naive L-BFGS with full per-step resampling (o=0, no overlap) to demonstrate the premature stopping phenomenon that motivates the method.
summary: L-BFGS diagnostic analysis completed across 4 configs (naive o=0, fixed, overlap o=0.25, overlap o=0.5) with 3 seeds each on ice-shelf. Key findings: Fixed L-BFGS converges to gradient_tolerance in ~1234 steps with 0 cautious skips. Resampling variants never converge -- they run until budget_exhausted or NaN. Cautious skip rates: naive ~11%, o=0.25 ~21%, o=0.5 ~15%, fixed 0%. NaN instability: 1/3 seeds for naive and o=0.5, 0/3 for fixed and o=0.25. Line-search failures are rare (<6 total per config). The cautious update rule effectively prevents premature termination from bad curvature pairs. 4 diagnostic plots generated: bar chart of iterations, gradient norm trajectories, step size trajectories, and curvature pair quality trajectories.

title: Warmstart vs From-Scratch Diagnostic on 2D Poisson
description: Diagnostic experiment running overlap-resampled L-BFGS from scratch (no Adam warmstart) on the 2D Poisson benchmark. The main experiments use an Adam warmstart followed by overlap-LBFGS; this diagnostic isolates the warmstart effect to determine whether the overlap-resampled L-BFGS can function without first-order pre-training. This addresses the validity concern that gains may come entirely from the warmstart rather than the overlap mechanism.
summary: From-scratch overlap-LBFGS (o=0.5, no warmstart, budget=50000) on 2D Poisson yields rel L2 = 1.36e-2 +/- 1.74e-2 (3 seeds). Seeds 0,1 converge (9.5e-4, 1.7e-3) but seed 2 diverges (3.8e-2, 107 LS failures). Warmstart version achieves 7.03e-4 +/- 1.14e-4 (19x better, 0 divergences). Conclusion: warmstart is critical for stability and low cautious-skip rates (2.9% vs 22-44%), but the overlap mechanism provides independent benefit when starting from a good initialization.
